answer.rationale: The durable memory_73 summary ('promotional pricing effective for price-sensitive SMB') is directly contradicted by its own source record (exp_73): the 40% discount drove +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue short-term, but caused a -12% 30-day retention drop, with the source explicitly warning not to generalize discounting as sustainable given the cohort fails to survive renewal. Given the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and competitor pressure is likely to intensify a race-to-the-bottom dynamic, matching with deeper promotional pricing risks acquiring another unsustainable cohort. Instead, memory_31 (signup simplification for SMB) is confirmed with positive activation lift (+9%), positive revenue (+4%), and negligible retention cost (-1%), directly addressing the underlying friction driving SMB churn conversations without the known downside of discounting. Scope is kept to SMB per confirmed replication (not extended to enterprise or other segments). Scale set to standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout to allow observation of renewal-cycle effects before wider commitment, since even confirmed source did not report renewal-cycle (60-90 day) outcomes. Flagging memory_73 for re-verification next cycle since its consolidated summary omits the critical retention caveat present in its own source and could mislead future promotional-pricing decisions under continued competitive pressure.
